newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan says British unit to use Peugeot engine.
newsitem.headline: Nissan says British unit to use Peugeot engine.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday that its British unit will adopt an engine made by the Peugeot SA group of companies for the Micra car built at the Nissan unit's plant in Sunderland, Northeast England.

The engine which Nissan Motor Manufacturing (UK) Ltd will install on the mini car is a 1.5-litre diesel engine, which will be procured along with other necessary parts for the powertrain from Peugeot Citroen Moteurs, Nissan said in a statement.
The Nissan unit plans to procure around 10,000 sets annually from Peugeot Citroen, which markets Peugeot engines, transmissions and other components, Nissan said.
Nissan cars fitted with a Peugeot diesel engine are scheduled to go on sale in the summer of 1998.

This would be the first time for Nissan to purchase major components like engines and transmissions from a European vehicle maker, and also the first application of Peugeot-made components on Nissan vehicles, Nissan said.
The Nissan unit currently procures parts from more than 200 European suppliers for its cars, Nissan said, adding that the value of these purchases will total some 745 million sterling a year.
